cycles.name: Foundation Forge
focuses: Build movement quality, spine and knee resilience, and a controlled aerobic base.
Re-groove bilateral strength patterns and establish baseline RPE awareness.

paragraphs: Ghazal, this first cycle is the platform everything else stands on. With 15 years of lifting behind you and a body that's carried lumbar and knee history, the job right now isn't to chase intensity — it's to re-teach your joints to move under load with complete control.
Focus mentally on precision over effort: every rep owned, every landing quiet, every brace intentional. This is where we earn the right to go heavy in Cycle 2.
outcomes: Cleaner squat mechanics under tempo-controlled load
A core that holds under rotation and anti-rotation demands
Noticeable drop in body fat from Zone 2 + interval work
Knees that feel stable and pain-free on plyometrics
Baseline RPE awareness across all main lifts
Restored shoulder balance for serve durability

cycles.name: Strength Engine
focuses: Drive maximal strength through moderate loads (RPE 7–8) with unilateral emphasis.
Introduce tempo-controlled plyometrics to prep tendons for court load.

paragraphs: Ghazal, welcome back. Last cycle was about teaching your body to move well under load. You started it well, then life got in the way. That's fine. We pick up where the plan says, we don't start over.
This block is about getting strong. Fewer reps, heavier feel, and a lot more work on one leg at a time. Week one is for finding your weights again, not chasing them. After that we push.
By the end you should feel it on court. Stronger off the first step and steadier when you're stretched wide. Your shoulder should hold up better on the smash too.
outcomes: Back squat stronger than where Cycle 1 finished
An overhead press you don't have to drop mid-set
Your first properly loaded hinge, done clean
Single-leg strength that holds in a wide stretch
Three new conditioning tools working on fat loss
Four sessions a week that actually happen

cycles.name: Power Translator
focuses: Convert strength to sport-specific power, rotational speed, and change-of-direction.
Layer in reactive plyos and shoulder ballistics tied to tennis mechanics.

teaser.subtitle: Strength is the price of speed.
paragraphs: Cycle 3 is where this strength turns into speed. The work gets faster and sharper, and all of it is built on what you do in the next five weeks.
You can't shortcut that one. Reactive work only pays off when the strength underneath it is real.
Build it now. Spend it later.

cycles.name: Metabolic Shift
focuses: Aggressive body composition phase through elevated volume conditioning and repeat-effort work.
Preserve strength with short, heavy exposures twice weekly.

cycles.name: Court-Ready Peak
focuses: Peak speed, agility, and on-court durability for match-quality output.
Taper volume, sharpen neural output, and bulletproof shoulders and low back.

cards.title: Your Knee, Your Rules
cards.body:
Your knee history is the one thing we build around this cycle. Before every Day 1, do 5 bodyweight squats and rate your knee 0 to 10. Anything above a 3 and you swap the box jumps for box step-ups that day. No debate, just swap.

What's fine is normal muscle burn, tired legs, and dull soreness that's gone in a day. What's not fine is sharp pain, anything down the side of the knee, or pain that gets worse as the set goes on instead of settling.

Here's what to do:

  • Mild and it fades: finish the set, write it in your log.
  • Building, or it changes how you move: stop that exercise, use the swap on the card, message me.
  • Sharp, new, radiating, or anything numb: stop the session and message me before your next one.

Telling me something hurts never costs you training. It gets you a different exercise, that's all.

cards.title: Week One Is For Finding Your Weights
cards.body:
You've had time away from the gym, so week one isn't about pushing. It's about finding what RPE 8 feels like again.

On a movement you know, start under what you think you can do and let the first set tell you. Comes up easy, add weight. Grinds, stay there or come down. On the new movements just start light. There's no prize for guessing right on set one.

After that it's simple. Hit the reps at or under the target RPE and you go up a small step next time. Miss reps, or the set feels harder than the number on the card, and you repeat that weight until it doesn't.

Dropping weight on a bad day isn't going backwards. It's the system working.

cards.title: Why Your Upper Day Changed
cards.body:
One thing jumps out of your Cycle 1 numbers. You pulled 110lb on the lat pulldown at RPE 6, and you had to come down from 20lb to 15lb on the overhead press. Your pulling is strong and your pressing is well behind it.

That gap matters for padel. The smash and everything overhead comes from the same place, and a weak press is where shoulders start complaining.

So Day 2 leads with pressing while you're fresh, and your overhead work is a landmine press now. The bar travels on an angle instead of straight up, which most shoulders prefer. Give it the focus you give the pulldown and it'll catch up fast.

cards.title: Sleep Is Your Biggest Lever
cards.body:
You told me 5 to 6 hours a night and stress at 9 out of 10. That's the real ceiling on this cycle, not the training.

I can't fix your stress and I won't pretend otherwise. Sleep is the one you can actually move. Getting to 7 hours would do more for your body composition and your strength than anything I could add to the program.

One thing to try. Pick a fixed time you stop looking at your phone and hold it for two weeks. Don't aim for perfect, aim for one extra hour.

This is also why you're on four days and not five. Five was too much last time.

cards.title: Protein At Every Meal
cards.body:
You said your eating has no real structure. We're not going to count everything, that never lasts. Start with protein at every meal and nothing else.

A palm-sized portion of chicken, meat, fish, eggs, yoghurt or lentils at each of your three meals. That's the whole instruction. It keeps you full, it protects your muscle while you lose fat, and it makes everything else easier.

Once it's automatic for a few weeks, tell me and we'll add the next piece. One habit at a time beats a full diet you drop in week two.

cards.title: Four Days Is The Program
cards.body:
Last time you had five days and you got through one week. This time four days is the whole program. Day 1, Day 2, Day 3, Day 4. Do those and you've done everything I asked.

Day 5 is optional and it's meant to be. It's a walk and some mobility. Take it on a good week, skip it on a bad one, and don't feel bad about skipping it.

Keep Day 1 and Day 4 at least a day apart, they're both heavy on your legs. Everything else you can move around your padel and your work.

Four sessions you actually do beats five you plan and miss.

cards.title: What Day 3 Is Really For
cards.body:
Day 3 looks nothing like last cycle and that's deliberate. The sled and the ropes give you a genuinely hard session with no pounding on your knees and almost no soreness the next day. That's what lets it sit between your two heavy leg days.

The structure is the other half. Short hard efforts with not quite enough rest is exactly what a padel point is. Learning to repeat that is worth more to you than one long steady session.

On the bike intervals your target is round 8 looking like round 1. If rounds 6 to 8 fall apart, you went too hard at the start.

cards.title: Period Week
cards.body:
Nothing here changes how I plan your training. This is just so you never have to work out what to do on a bad day.

On those days, here's the version of each session:

  • Full as written: Day 3 and Day 5. The sled, ropes, bike and the walk all tend to help with cramping, so don't skip them.
  • Cut to 2 sets and go lighter: back squat, dumbbell bench press, Romanian deadlift, Bulgarian split squat. Move the pattern, don't grind it.
  • Skip for those days: the Pallof press, side plank and Copenhagen plank. Hard bracing through the middle is what tends to feel worst.

Log it as done. A modified session is still a session.

cards.title: What You Already Showed Me
cards.body:
Two things from Cycle 1 I want you to know I noticed.

Your lat pulldown was 110lb for 8 reps at RPE 6. At your bodyweight that's genuinely strong, and it wasn't close to your limit. You've got a good engine in your back and we're going to use it this cycle.

The other one is that you told me the lateral step-down was too hard instead of quietly skipping it. That's exactly what I need from you. It's gone, and there's a reverse lunge in its place. Keep doing that.

cards.title: Adjusting On A Rough Day
cards.body:
Some weeks your sleep and stress will make the numbers on the card look silly. On a low-readiness day, take 1 off every RPE in the session, but never go below 6. Six is the lowest the app lets you log, so anything already sitting at 6 just stays at 6.

If you're short on time or energy, the minimum that still counts is the first power move plus the first main lift. Do those two and log it. That's a session.

You can move the days around your padel and your work. If you train padel and gym on the same day, do the gym after padel, or leave 4 to 6 hours between them. If neither works, run the minimum above and keep the main lift at RPE 6.
